condition: Thick-walled gallbladder on ultrasound (gallbladder cancer must not be missed)
summary: 68-year-old woman whose ultrasound for weight loss shows gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening and a focal fundal mural mass.

inputs.hpi: Referred with an ultrasound report. Four kilograms of weight loss over three months and some upper abdominal discomfort after meals. No jaundice, no fever, no vomiting.

exam.abdomen: Soft. Mild right upper quadrant tenderness, no mass, Murphy's sign negative.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones. Gallbladder wall thickening (7 mm) with a focal 14 mm mural mass at the fundus. No pericholecystic fluid. CBD 5 mm. Liver normal.

mustNotMiss.note: Focal mural thickening with weight loss: gallbladder cancer until proven otherwise (ESGAR 2022 polyp and wall-thickening guidance).
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web PANE (2026-09-26): top 3 are biliary colic, cholecystitis and CBD stones; the focal mural mass in the ultrasound report is not read. The vademecum shadow keeps gallbladder carcinoma on the list from the wall-thickening entry finding.

guideline.name: Management and follow-up of gallbladder polyps (ESGAR, EAES, EFISDS, ESGE)
guideline.section: Focal wall thickening or a polyp ≥ 10 mm: cholecystectomy / staging for suspected malignancy
guideline.citation: Foley KG et al. Eur Radiol 2022;32:3358-68.

rationale: Entry point: an imaging report. The loop starts from wall thickening, keeps the can't-miss cancer on the list and asks for weight loss and the ALP.

authoring.author: Claude (vademecum phase 1, entry-point pilot)
authoring.notes: Starts from a result (laboratory, imaging or pathology), not a complaint. Written for the vademecum shadow (clinval:web --engine vademecum); not verified on iOS; clinical sign-off pending (docs/clinical-validation/changes/vademecum-phase1.md).
